cabecalho-safetensors.d: The start of a .safetensors file: 8 bytes holding the size N (a 64-bit little-endian integer) followed by N bytes of JSON with the dtype, shape and data_offsets of every tensor. You can read it without downloading the data.

range-request.d: An HTTP request with the Range: bytes=a-b header, which asks for just one slice of the file. Used in triage to read the safetensors headers of ~1 GB shards without downloading them.

pre-sharding.d: A checkpoint saved already sliced for a specific tensor-parallel degree (in MiMo, tp_size: 4 in the fused QKV). Running at a different TP requires reassembling the slices and, sometimes, requantizing.

diffkv.d: Attention in which K and V have different head dimensions (in MiMo, 192 and 128). Common kernels assume head_size_v == head_size; vLLM has dedicated backends (TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV, FLASH_ATTN_DIFFKV).

attention-sink.d: An extra learned logit in the attention softmax, one per head, that gives attention a place to “dump” probability mass. It stabilizes short windows; in MiMo only the SWA layers have a sink.

memoria-unificada.d: CPU and GPU use the same physical memory pool (LPDDR5X on the GB10). The OS, the page cache and the host processes compete with vLLM for the same bytes.

gmu.d: The fraction of CUDA-visible memory that vLLM may use for weights, activations, CUDA graphs and KV cache. On the GB10 each 0.01 is worth ~1.2 GiB taken from the host’s headroom; the alternative is to pin the pool with --kv-cache-memory.

alocador-kv-hibrido.d: The part of vLLM that groups layers with the same KV type (global, window, Mamba, drafter) and gives each group pages of the same size. Incomplete groups waste space: in MiMo, 9 global layers in groups of 5 take up 10 slots (+11%).

kld.d: \( D_{KL}(P\|Q)=\sum_t P(t)\log\frac{P(t)}{Q(t)} \): how far the candidate Q’s next-token distribution strays from the reference P, in nats. The preferred metric for comparing quantizations; perplexity alone hides errors that cancel out.

w4a16-w4a8-w4a4.d: Weight bits / activation bits inside the GEMM. Fewer activation bits give more compute throughput (especially in prefill) and more error. In MiMo, Marlin MXFP4 in W4A16 or W4A8 (VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE=fp8).

tensor-parallel.d: Splitting each of the model’s matrices across GPUs (by columns or rows), with all-reduces to combine the results: two per layer in a Transformer block. It requires heads, KV heads and widths to divide by the TP degree.

overlay.d: A .py file of the installed package replaced by a bind-mount (-v file:target:ro), generated from the pinned image’s own file by a fail-closed patch. It fixes the engine without rebuilding the image.

fail-closed.d: The property of a patch that, faced with any surprise (a missing or duplicated anchor, a different hash), aborts with a clear error instead of producing a half-modified file. It is the opposite of failing silently.

paridade-truncada.d: A numerical test that compares the engine and the reference (HF) with the same first N layers of the model (--hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": N}'), via KLD and top-1 agreement of the logprobs. It isolates kernel and loading errors without having to run the whole model in the reference.

tool-call-storm.d: A failure in which the model repeats the same tool call dozens or hundreds of times. In MiMo it showed up with the near-greedy decoding of vLLM’s defaults; --generation-config auto and the MOPD checkpoint mitigate it.

aceitacao-especulativa.d: How many drafted tokens the target accepts per step (and the per-position rate, which decays with position). Read from /metrics as Δaccepted/Δdrafts; together with the step cost, it is what decides k.

needle-test.d: A long-context test: it hides a fact (the “needle”) at various depths of a long text and asks about it at the end. It catches mask and window bugs that short prompts do not reveal.

teto-de-banda.d: The upper bound on a single stream’s tok/s without speculation: memory bandwidth ÷ bytes read per step (active experts + everything that is dense). For MiMo at TP2, ~273 GB/s ÷ ~6.4 GB ≈ 43 tok/s; in practice, 50–65% of that.

ab-a.d: An experiment design: baseline, change and baseline again, with repetitions and a median per arm. It separates the effect of the change from the system’s drift (page cache, autotune, temperature); you accept only if B beats both baselines.

plugin-out-of-tree.d: A Python package with an entry point in the vllm.general_plugins group that registers models, quantization methods or ops without forking vLLM (ModelRegistry.register_model("Arch", "package.module:Class")).

mopd.d: A post-training stage that distills several specialized teachers on the student’s own samples (on-policy); the card describes the MOPD2 version as Multi-Prefix Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation. The MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD checkpoint is the RL one with that extra stage: same architecture, same config and same drafter, different weights.
